findings.evidenceJa: わたしの方針には逆らえない
findings.governingReading: The geas prevents Shirou opposing Rin’s chosen course of action.
findings.explanation: The English weakens a rule of obedience to Rin’s policy into generic inability to interfere.

findings.highlight: given me the right to decide
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=わたし char=2]他人に決定権を委ねるべきじゃなかった
findings.governingReading: Rin says Shirou should not have entrusted decision-making authority to another person, with “me” supplied as the ruby reading.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only Rin as referent and deletes the broader other-person principle encoded by the written text.

findings.evidenceJa: 心臓が、一際大きく拡縮する
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s heart contracts and expands with exceptional force or amplitude.
findings.explanation: The English changes the heart’s physical expansion and contraction into audible loudness.

findings.governingReading: The object beside Shirou’s heart is a restraint called an oath.
findings.explanation: The English deletes both the restraint’s name and its conceptual connection to his vow.

findings.highlight: you chose to be my servant
findings.evidenceJa: 従者になる事を選んだ
findings.governingReading: Rin says Shirou chose to become her subordinate or follower rather than an equal collaborator.
findings.explanation: Using “servant” inside Fate’s class system risks falsely equating contractual subordination with becoming a Servant.

findings.highlight: I can’t even tell her to wait
findings.evidenceJa: 待て、という声さえ出せない
findings.governingReading: Shirou is physically unable to produce even the voice that would say “wait.”
findings.explanation: The English communicates failure but drops the bodily inability to voice the word.

findings.governingReading: Rin’s figure disappears from Shirou’s sight.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Shirou’s immobilized visual experience with neutral departure.

findings.highlight: I fight the binding, hoping that it’s not too late
findings.evidenceJa: 一刻も早く動けるようにともがいて
findings.governingReading: Shirou struggles to make his body move again at the earliest possible instant.
findings.explanation: The English changes urgency of bodily recovery into fear that an unstated deadline has passed.

findings.evidenceJa: 痺れていた体に、本来の自由が戻ってくれた
findings.governingReading: His numbed body abruptly regains its natural freedom of movement.
findings.explanation: The English omits the numbness and the sense of bodily freedom being restored to its proper state.

findings.highlight: because there’s no longer a need to hold me here
findings.evidenceJa: 反対していた理由が、既に失われたからではないのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou infers that his body became free because the reason he opposed Rin has already been lost—meaning Sakura may already be dead.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes an external need to restrain him, deleting the bad end’s devastating causal realization.

findings.evidenceJa: 行き場を無くした心が折れる
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s heart or spirit, left with nowhere to go, breaks.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the collapse to cognition and loses the emotional-spiritual image.

findings.highlight: It’s a new path that I can’t yield to anyone
findings.evidenceJa: それは新しい、誰にも譲れない道標だ
findings.governingReading: Protecting Sakura is a new guidepost or moral compass that Shirou will yield to no one.
findings.explanation: The English changes the principle that guides his way into the path itself.

findings.highlight: lost the person on whom I’d depended
findings.governingReading: Shirou has lost that new anchor or point of support.
findings.explanation: The English concretizes the figurative support as a person and adds emotional dependence.
